THE PODCAST YOU CAN READ / 01

We came to
study kanji.
Then things got
competitive.

Five microphones, one League and nobody willing to lose. Welcome to Kanjidon Radio.

Join the episode ↓
Who’s up for a battle?

Editorial script: characters and dialogue created by our editorial team, rather than drawn from recorded interviews.

MIC / 01Nico

“I’m not competitive.” Sure.

MIC / 02Bea

Her collection is an exhibition.

MIC / 03Marta

On the hunt for the next stamp.

MIC / 04Leo

Starting with the basics. Starting strong.

MIC / 05Sara

If she doesn’t like it, she’ll tell you.

Editorial script, no audio.
00 / KANJIDON RADIO

Mics on

[A chair scrapes. A phone goes face down on the table. Another, suspiciously, doesn’t.]

KANJIDON

Welcome. Today we have five guests who take kanji very seriously. Everything else, we’ll see. There’s Nico, of “I’m not competitive” fame; Bea, who wants every card; Marta, who can sniff out a hidden stamp; Leo, who’s starting with the basics; and Sara, who’ll tell us straight away if she doesn’t like something.

NICO

I never said I wasn’t competitive.

BEA

You said it right before asking us our ranks.

NICO

I was getting to know you. Name, rank, weaknesses. The basics.

KANJIDON

Excellent. We’re off to just the right start.

01 / KANJIDON RADIO

“Wait. I can battle with kanji?”

KANJIDON

Since Nico already has a file on everyone, let’s start with the League: online battles, the leaderboard, ranks. Do you remember the first time you opened it?

NICO

I thought: no, hang on a second. I can challenge other people to kanji battles online and move up the ranks? As in, the kanji I’m reviewing actually help me in a battle? That was it. That was the exact moment you had me. I sat up straight on the sofa. I was about to answer some questions, but in my head it was already the final.

SARA

Yeah, the first time I thought the same thing: so there’s actually another person on the other side? They could be halfway around the world, and we’re doing the same challenge. That’s brilliant. Then the question comes up and all I can think is: please, I know this one.

NICO

I skip straight to that part. And when I know the answer, you can hear me halfway around the world too.

LEO

See, before getting as excited as Nico, I wanted to know whether I could keep up. Being able to choose a league for my level really stood out. They go from N5 to N1, so there’s a path through the challenge. I don’t have to know everything before I can feel part of the game.

KANJIDON

And for anyone starting from scratch, the N5 League at rank E begins with kana. Kanji come in as you move up the ranks.

LEO

Exactly. I was convinced I’d jump in and get an educational smack in the face. Instead I thought: okay, I can start here too. And that first rank-up feels ridiculously good.

BEA

It’s how it all fits together. Your level, online opponents, a rank to aim for. A Japanese challenge with people from all over the world. I’d never come across anything like it, done this way.

MARTA

And finally, “I’m preparing for battle” is something I can say while studying on the sofa.

NICO

The League is awesome. I’m not looking for a fancier word. I just love battling. I love that moment when the question appears and you have to be ready. And I love having a rank ahead of me to go after. I see it there and think: all right, I’m coming for you. Maybe not today, but I’m coming.

KANJIDON

So, calm reflection, contemplation…

NICO

Later. First there’s someone ahead of me on the leaderboard, and we need to sort that out.

02 / KANJIDON RADIO

The rank goes up. So does the volume.

KANJIDON

So that next rank stays in your head even after you close the app. But what actually brings you back? Winning?

NICO

That too. I’m not going to get philosophical: winning feels amazing. But what surprises me is the bit before. I feel like doing a quiz, reviewing readings, sorting out that thing I always mix up. I want to go into the next challenge a little better prepared.

BEA

He calls it “sorting out that thing”. I heard him say, “That kanji and I are settling this today.”

NICO

We had unfinished business. I’d got it wrong twice. I wanted to be ready for round three.

LEO

I like that even a small step up counts. To someone further along, my rank might be nothing special. To me it’s: hey, I made it. With what I knew, from where I started.

SARA

Yeah, I’m happy when I move up too, even if Nico immediately asks how many points I have. Let me enjoy my thirty seconds, will you? I’m still learning, and I’ve already got a win under my belt.

MARTA

Then the leaderboard resets every month. That makes me want to jump back in. Fresh start, let’s see how far I get.

KANJIDON

And when you lose?

NICO

I become a very mature person.

BEA

He puts his phone down and stares at the ceiling.

NICO

I’m processing. Then I look back at what I got wrong. Unfortunately, the ceiling doesn’t know the readings.

SARA

I go back to the one I was sure I knew. That’s the one that annoys me most. I’m like: no, hang on, why is this answer wrong? And I’m not happy until I understand the difference.

LEO

And when you recognise it in a quiz later, it feels twice as good. It’s not like you suddenly know everything. But that little piece is there now.

“I feel like reviewing because I want to go into the next challenge a little better prepared.” · Nico
03 / KANJIDON RADIO

Bea was only going to open one pack

KANJIDON

So you go from battling back to reviewing. Bea, you’ve gone back to your collection instead: you’ve had it open this entire conversation.

BEA

Because look at the horse card. Properly look at it. The mountain behind it, the colours, the illustration. I was supposed to learn 馬, and now I have very strong opinions on how to display it.

MARTA

She doesn’t collect. She curates an exhibition.

BEA

Someone has to. They’re gorgeous, seriously. The horse, the river, the tree… I love opening a pack, seeing what I get, finding the card in my collection. It’s a little burst of joy every time.

KANJIDON

And where does the kanji fit into all this?

BEA

It’s why I go back to the card. I look at the picture, read, listen to the pronunciation. Then the quizzes tell me whether I actually remember it. Because “that’s pretty” and “I know the answer” are two different things. Unfortunately, my excellent taste can’t answer for me.

NICO

Can confirm. You can have a gorgeous card and still get the reading wrong in battle. Speaking from experience. Let’s not go there.

SARA

Bea’s right about the artwork, though. I open the cards just to look at them too. I like that you’ve put care into the ones you find right at the start as well. You don’t need some incredibly rare find to go: oh, that’s lovely.

BEA

Thank you. Now, back to the horse.

04 / KANJIDON RADIO

Marta and the lost property department

KANJIDON

Let’s stay with collections but switch objects. Marta, alongside cards, you’re hunting for stamps.

MARTA

I didn’t see the stamps coming at all. I open that section and think: sorry, there’s another collection in here? There’s a daruma. There’s ramen. There’s Tokyo Tower. Right, cancel everything, I have things to do.

LEO

What things?

MARTA

Investigate.

KANJIDON

The hunt is on.

MARTA

Yes, but the best part is they’re not just pictures to look at. There are stamps to unlock by playing, making progress, exploring. You see the ones you’re missing, read a hint and think: hmm. There’s something to try here.

BEA

I started with the cards. She got me to open the stamps page. I thought I’d seen everything, and it turned out I’d missed an entire collection. Thanks, Marta. Really, thank you.

MARTA

And some are linked to battles too. So I go back to the League with two things in mind: I want to climb, and I want to see what else I can unlock. I’m having an absolute blast.

NICO

Finally, a serious statement of intent.

05 / KANJIDON RADIO

Someone’s already up to something in Live

KANJIDON

Speaking of discovering things: in Live, you can also see what everyone else is doing. Who wins a battle, who moves up a rank, who unlocks a stamp. Do you look at it?

MARTA

I do, loads. I see a stamp I don’t have and tap through to find out which one it is. Sometimes I came in for something completely different and end up hunting for that instead. That’s how I realise how much I’ve still got to discover.

BEA

I stop at the packs and cards. Obviously. I like seeing what other people get. It immediately makes me want to open my own collection and check.

SARA

I like seeing that people are playing right then. Someone finishes a story, someone else wins a battle. Before, I’d do my quiz and close the app. Now I pop into Live sometimes to see what’s happening.

KANJIDON

And there are posts for making friends, finding challengers or asking for help with a stamp.

MARTA

I absolutely love the stamp part. If I can’t work out how to unlock one, I can ask someone who has it. I’m happy to do some detective work, but after a while I give in and ask.

NICO

I heard “finding challengers”. I’ll catch up on the rest later.

BEA

We just described a community to him and he saw a list of opponents.

NICO

With affection, though. First we make friends, then we find out who knows their kanji.

LEO

At least now we know why he asked our ranks as soon as we arrived.

06 / KANJIDON RADIO

“Okay, but now I need to know how it ends”

KANJIDON

Between the League and Live, Nico would have us battling all day. Sara, you sometimes switch things up completely and open the stories.

SARA

Yeah, because at some point I’ve had enough competing and want something to read. I open a story, listen and try to follow the text. At first I go back quite a lot, then I get into it and want to know how it ends. That’s when I keep going longer than I meant to.

LEO

You’re the one who says “no spoilers” even about the exercises.

SARA

Because you’re always saying, “Have you seen the bit where…” No, Leo. I’m reading it now. Let me get there.

KANJIDON

What feels most rewarding?

SARA

When I recognise a word from the cards without immediately opening the translation. I think: wait, I know this one. Then I might get stuck again on the very next sentence and have to listen again, obviously. But I can tell something has stuck, and it makes me want to keep going.

BEA

And the illustrations make you want to stay there too. I open everything partly just to see how it’s drawn.

NICO

So we can confirm you’re in charge of image quality control.

BEA

With great dedication.

LEO

For me, being able to switch is what works. I do quizzes, try writing, go back to the cards. Then a story. Then maybe I feel ready for a battle. I don’t have to be in the same mood every time I open Kanjidon.

07 / KANJIDON RADIO

Excuse me, what about DoDon?

KANJIDON

We’ve talked loads about the artwork and forgotten someone. DoDon: what do you make of our mascot?

BEA

Finally. I love him. You took a deep-sea fish, gave him that face and said: perfect, he can oversee all this chaos. The little light, the tiny teeth, that “I know something you don’t” look. He’s brilliant.

SARA

He makes me laugh because he always looks so sure of himself. I’m still trying to remember a reading, and he already looks like he’s won.

MARTA

Basically Nico, with fins.

NICO

Finally, a mascot with the right attitude. I’d have him next to me during battles. I answer, he gives the opponent a dirty look.

KANJIDON

You want to hire DoDon as your coach?

NICO

As my cornerman. I do my training in the quizzes. All I ask of him is to keep believing in me while I stare at the ceiling.

BEA

I want him on my desk. Next to the horse.

LEO

You’re already decorating with cards from the app.

BEA

I told you I liked the artwork.

08 / KANJIDON RADIO

Mics off. More or less.

KANJIDON

Last round. One thing you’d say to someone who’s never opened Kanjidon. Just one, Nico.

NICO

Try the League. Pick your level, join an online challenge, then tell me moving up a rank doesn’t leave you grinning like an idiot. For me, it’s the best thing in the app.

BEA

Open a pack. You’ll understand why I keep talking about the horse.

MARTA

When you think you’ve seen everything, check the stamps.

SARA

Try a story and see how much you can follow. Then come and tell me how it ends, because I might still be halfway through.

LEO

Don’t wait until you feel good enough to have fun.

[For once, nobody interrupts him.]

KANJIDON

We’re keeping that one. Thank you all, this has been brilliant. We can switch off now.

NICO

Yeah. Who’s up for a battle?

BEA

Hang on, let me finish this.

KANJIDON

Are you still looking at the horse?

BEA

It’s a great horse.

End of episode. The challenge continues.

Open packs. Collect. Remember.

KANJIDON RADIO / END OF EPISODE

The mic is yours.

Where do you stand? League, Live, cards, stamps or stories?
